Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our procurement checklist we've attached an initial set of redlines to the Private Deployment Addendum (PDF). Two items we need to lock down to get to legal sign-off:

1) Operator witness / sample access: we need language that guarantees at least one witnessed snapshot and acceptance window during deployment and a short-term read-only session for our auditors.
2) Evidence delivery timing: we need an explicit schedule for delivering a forensic snapshot and checksum within 14 days of go-live (with an option for our team to schedule an on-site witness within 30 days).

I've attached Medivate_Redlines_Private_Addendum.pdf and a quick Operator_Witness_Spec.xlsx that summarizes the types of artifacts we'd expect (sha256 checksums, snapshot retention metadata, and a short list of test lifts). Can you confirm these are feasible for Redwood's Private deployment model and suggest any alternative wording that preserves your operational limits?

Also looping in procurement to keep timelines visible. We are targeting PO issuance by 2026-08-25 if the addendum is agreed.

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood to provide proposed redline responses by EOD Thursday (8/13)
- Short sync (30 min) if there are material changes to the witness scope

Appreciate the quick turnaround,

Claire Dawson

Claire —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear checklist. Short answer: yes, we can support a witnessed snapshot and the short proof delivery you're asking for, with a few operational guardrails I want to propose so we set expectations correctly. High-level comments below; Rishi (legal) will add contract language suggestions.

Operational guardrails we propose:
- Witness session: Redwood can provide one witnessed snapshot session (remote video + shared console) during the first 30 days post-deployment. This includes a read-only proof run and checksum verification. On-site witnessing is possible but treated as a professional services engagement (costs + travel).
- Snapshot delivery: we can produce a verifiable forensic snapshot (read-only image + sha256 manifest) within 10 business days of a confirmed go-live. If additional copies are requested, we will coordinate delivery windows with your security team.
- Scope: snapshots cover the deployed inference stack and customer-specific model files; they do not include proprietary internal runtime telemetry (we can provide summarized runtime artifact logs instead).

Attached is a quick MAP (Mutual Action Plan) draft that aligns to your PO timeline. If this looks good we'll draft specific contract language for the addendum around the witness window, acceptance criteria, and a limited license carve-out for the snapshot evidence.

Propose a quick sync Wednesday 8/12 at 10:00 PT to walk the redlines and MAP — want to make sure procurement is comfortable with the on-site vs remote options.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Senior Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Claire / Kimberly —

Looping in from Legal. I reviewed the PDF and sketched suggested language for three areas so procurement can move forward without creating an open-ended obligation for Redwood:

1) Witness session (proposed clause): "Customer may request one remote witness session within 30 days of go-live. Redwood will facilitate a read-only demonstration of snapshot creation and provide verification artifacts (sha256 manifests). Any on-site witnessing shall be mutually agreed and invoiced separately as professional services."

2) Evidence retention and license (proposed clause): "Redwood will deliver a one-time, customer-specific read-only forensic snapshot and accompanying verification artifacts within ten (10) business days following a confirmed go-live. The snapshot is provided solely for Customer’s internal audit purposes; Customer may not use, distribute, or modify Redwood proprietary runtime components contained in the snapshot."

3) Liability/acceptance carveout: include limited acceptance window (15 business days) for Customer to validate snapshot artifacts; after which the snapshot is deemed accepted absent timely written objections tied to the verification artifacts.

I've attached a redline (inline comments) to the addendum — see the keyed changes and the proposed wording for the three clauses above. Kimberly — if the on-site option is important to Medivate, we should include a short pricing paragraph in the MAP (to avoid delays).

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the draft clauses — very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- On-site witnessing is something our auditors may request for regulated customers; can you provide a ballpark for the professional services day rate and typical travel terms so we can include cost planning in the PO?

On timing — we still hope to sign the MSA + Order Form no later than 2026-08-25. We have legal on standby (Eric is cc'd). Claire
